sections.title: The Promise of God's Presence
observations: In this section, God reassures Moses of His presence as they journey to the Promised Land. God emphasizes that His presence is what distinguishes His people from others. This highlights the importance of divine guidance in the life of believers.
Moses intercedes for the people, reminding God of His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. This shows the relational aspect of God's covenant and the role of intercession in prayer.

sections.title: Moses' Desire to See God's Glory
observations: Moses expresses a deep desire to know God more intimately, asking to see His glory. This reflects a profound spiritual hunger that should be present in every believer's life.

God's response indicates that while Moses cannot see His full glory and live, He will reveal His goodness and name to him. This teaches us about the nature of God and the limitations of human understanding.

sections.title: God's Revelation and Assurance
observations: God places Moses in the cleft of the rock and covers him with His hand as He passes by. This imagery illustrates God's protection and the idea that we can only comprehend so much of His glory.

The proclamation of God's name reveals His character: merciful, gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love. This is foundational for understanding God's nature and His dealings with humanity.

importantVerses.commentary: God's promise, 'My presence will go with you, and I will give you rest,' emphasizes the importance of God's presence in providing peace and assurance to His people.
God's declaration, 'I will make all my goodness pass before you,' highlights the revelation of God's character and His goodness towards His people.

questions: What does it mean for God's presence to go with us today?
How can we cultivate a deeper desire to know God as Moses did?
In what ways does God's revelation of His character impact our understanding of His relationship with us?
